import pandas as pd
from typing import Dict

def run(inputs: Dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> Dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    target_snapshot = inputs["target_snapshot"].copy()
    cdc_events = inputs["cdc_events"].copy()
    watermark = inputs["watermark"].copy()
    
    # Extract the watermark high_ts (single row)
    high_ts = watermark["high_ts"].iloc[0]
    
    # Filter events: keep only those with event_ts > high_ts
    filtered_events = cdc_events[cdc_events["event_ts"] > high_ts].copy()
    
    # If no new events, return target snapshot unchanged
    if filtered_events.empty:
        return {"new_snapshot": target_snapshot}
    
    # Sort by product_id, event_ts (ascending), then event_seq (ascending)
    # This ensures that when we take the last row per product_id,
    # we get the latest event by (event_ts, event_seq)
    filtered_events = filtered_events.sort_values(
        by=["product_id", "event_ts", "event_seq"],
        ascending=[True, True, True]
    )
    
    # Keep only the latest event per product_id
    latest_events = filtered_events.drop_duplicates(
        subset=["product_id"],
        keep="last"
    )
    
    # Separate deletes from inserts/updates
    deletes = latest_events[latest_events["op"] == "D"]["product_id"].tolist()
    upserts = latest_events[latest_events["op"].isin(["I", "U"])]
    
    # Remove deleted products from target snapshot
    new_snapshot = target_snapshot[~target_snapshot["product_id"].isin(deletes)].copy()
    
    # Process upserts: update existing or insert new
    for _, row in upserts.iterrows():
        product_id = row["product_id"]
        
        # Check if product exists in new_snapshot
        exists = product_id in new_snapshot["product_id"].values
        
        if exists:
            # Update existing product
            mask = new_snapshot["product_id"] == product_id
            new_snapshot.loc[mask, "name"] = row["name"]
            new_snapshot.loc[mask, "price"] = row["price"]
            new_snapshot.loc[mask, "last_event_ts"] = row["event_ts"]
        else:
            # Insert new product
            new_row = pd.DataFrame({
                "product_id": [product_id],
                "name": [row["name"]],
                "price": [row["price"]],
                "last_event_ts": [row["event_ts"]]
            })
            new_snapshot = pd.concat([new_snapshot, new_row], ignore_index=True)
    
    # Ensure column order and types match target_snapshot
    new_snapshot = new_snapshot[["product_id", "name", "price", "last_event_ts"]].copy()
    new_snapshot["product_id"] = new_snapshot["product_id"].astype("int64")
    new_snapshot["name"] = new_snapshot["name"].astype("object")
    new_snapshot["price"] = new_snapshot["price"].astype("float64")
    new_snapshot["last_event_ts"] = new_snapshot["last_event_ts"].astype("datetime64[us]")
    
    # Reset index for clean output
    new_snapshot = new_snapshot.reset_index(drop=True)
    
    return {"new_snapshot": new_snapshot}
